title: Surrender of Cover After the Free-Look Period, Travel Protection Plans
content:
After the free-look period a policyholder on the Travel Protection Plans may still give up cover, and the
plan's mid-term share of the unearned premium is returned with it.

## The rule

1. The plan's mid-term share of the unearned premium is returned.
2. Unearned premium is measured by the whole days of cover remaining out of the whole days of cover bought,
   counted from the day after the cancellation takes effect.
3. Nothing is returned on a plan whose mid-term share is zero, and nothing is returned once any claim has been
   filed under the policy, whatever the plan.
4. The policy fee and any cancel-for-any-reason upgrade premium are never part of the unearned premium.
5. Cover ends at the moment the cancellation is confirmed, and an incident occurring afterwards is not covered
   even where the journey continues.
6. A cancelled policy is never reinstated. A traveller who changes their mind buys fresh cover, subject to the
   underwriting rules as they then stand.

## The measure of unearned premium

| Element | What it is |
|---|---|
| The denominator | The whole days of cover bought |
| The numerator | The whole days of cover remaining, counted from the day after the cancellation takes effect |
| Outside the measure | The policy fee, and any cancel-for-any-reason upgrade premium |

## Points of judgement

Where a claim has already been filed under the policy, nothing is returned, and the size of the plan's mid-term
share makes no difference to that answer. Where the plan's mid-term share is zero, nothing is returned even
though most of the journey is still to come. Where cover is given up in the middle of a journey the traveller
means to finish, the journey may continue but an incident occurring after the moment of confirmation is not
covered, and the traveller who then wants cover again buys a fresh policy rather than having this one restored.
